name: Vaidyaratnam P. S. Varier’s Arya Vaidya Sala (Kottakkal)
tagline: Century-old world‑famous Ayurvedic hospital, manufacturing and wellness pilgrimage
summary: Founded in 1902, Kottakkal Arya Vaidya Sala is a global centre for classical Ayurveda — hospitals, GMP factories, research, college and a major destination for panchakarma and chronic-care patients.
description: Arya Vaidya Sala (AVS) at Kottakkal is a charitable Ayurvedic institution founded by Vaidyaratnam P.S. Varier in 1902 that grew into a multi‑unit organisation combining treatment, manufacturing and research.

The campus includes the historic charitable hospital, a modern Ayurvedic Hospital & Research Centre, GMP manufacturing units, a medicinal plant centre, publications and an Ayurveda college — making Kottakkal a pilgrimage town for people seeking authentic classical therapies.

Patients come from India and abroad for expert consultation, full in‑patient panchakarma and Kerala specialist therapies; AVS also engages in clinical research and quality testing and holds NABH accreditation for its hospitals.
highlights: Founded 1902 by Vaidyaratnam P.S. Varier — one of modern Ayurveda’s landmark institutions.
Comprehensive inpatient panchakarma and Kerala specialist therapies in NABH‑accredited hospitals.
Large GMP factories producing hundreds of classical formulations.
Centre for medicinal plants, research, publications and an Ayurveda college.
Newer 120‑bed AH&RC (Kottakkal East / Kavathikalam) opened in 2023.

sections.heading: Background
body: Vaidyaratnam P.S. Varier established Arya Vaidya Sala in Kottakkal in 1902 to standardise authentic Ayurvedic medicines and provide organised clinical care. Over the 20th century AVS added a teaching pathshala, manufacturing units and hospital complexes, and it remains rooted in classical texts while adopting modern quality systems.

AVS runs charitable services alongside paid hospital facilities, publishes Ayurvedic literature, maintains herb gardens and a museum, and has collaborated on clinical and scientific research programs.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Consult with an AVS physician for an individualized plan — common offerings include detailed Ayurvedic diagnosis (including pulse and clinical assessment), panchakarma courses, specialty Kerala therapies and long‑term chronic‑care programs. Inpatient stays include physician supervision, therapies and patient diet guidelines.

On the campus visitors can see the museum, the temple consecrated by P.S. Varier, the herbal gardens and the production/quality facilities (visible from external areas); AVS also runs cultural activity (PSV Natyasangham) and a college where classical training continues.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Book consultations or inpatient programs in advance — AVS provides e‑consultation and room booking through its hospital contacts. Expect an initial physician consultation before admission; medical visa is required for foreign patients and some admission formalities apply.

Accommodation ranges from wards to suites; the Kottakkal campus has canteen, library, yoga and physiotherapy facilities. Confirm treatment plan, duration and tariff with AVS before travel as programs commonly run for multiple weeks.

latest.text: AVS published a public tender notice for works at the Kottakkal campus (site tender document dated 25 Feb 2026).
A new 120‑bed Ayurvedic Hospital & Research Centre (Kottakkal East, Kavathikalam) began operation on 3 July 2023, expanding AVS inpatient capacity.

visitorInfo.bestTime: October–March (cooler, drier months suit panchakarma and convalescence)
visitorInfo.howToReach: Kottakkal Bus Stand is about 350 m from the AVS area; nearest major rail head Tirur ≈ 16 km; Calicut (Kozhikode) International Airport ≈ 26 km. Local taxis and buses connect to AVS. (Confirm schedules before travel.)
etiquette: Book physician consultation and, for inpatient programs, room reservations well in advance.
Medical visa is required for foreign nationals seeking inpatient treatment—confirm documentation with AVS.
Follow AVS dietary and lifestyle guidance during treatment; alcohol, smoking and non‑vegetarian food are restricted in hospital premises.
Carry copies of medical records and any medication list for the initial consultation.
